ABOUT THIS LITTLE TOWN

Pictures first. Words next.

Look at the scene, notice the action, and connect it straight to English. No translation step.

See it. Say it. Remember it.

  1. Explore a scene. Tap a dot or a word. Look at its close-up or little picture story.
  2. Listen, say it aloud and read the short English example.
  3. Choose “Picture only”. Try to remember the word before you reveal it.
  4. Play a picture quiz or try spelling. Come back another day to make the memory last.
Grade 4 · Book 1 · 142 words and phrases

This collection follows Words to use, pages 87–89, in Shanghai Education Press English, Grade 4, Book 1, five-four system, 2024-approved edition. It includes both new and recurring words; their original colour coding was unavailable in the public text. The matching new Book 2 is not yet verified and is not included.

A gentle way to review

“I know it” marks a word as familiar. Correct answers on separate days raise its memory level. Level 2 counts as remembered. Review intervals are 1, 3 and 7 days; a missed word returns to your review list. Repeating answers on the same day does not increase the level.

Made for this little world

Illustrations, picture stories and example sentences are original learning aids. Some pictures are visual associations, not textbook illustrations. IPA uses British English. Audio uses the English voices available on your device. Progress is stored only in your current browser, without an account or automatic syncing.
